messages.author: 5d3368b7e537b5dc
messages.subject: Workaround for broken scales = "free"?
parts:
Howdy,

I seem to have hit upon a case where the scales="free" argument to
facet_grid does absolutely nothing. See the reproducible example below
-- ideally, the x-axis of each facet should be different.

I searched the mailing list and learned that scales="free" does not
work for non-cartesian coordinates, so can I assume that's my problem
here, since my y-axis is a factor? I would have thought it became
cartesian "under the hood", or something, i.e., those y-axis ticks are
underlyingly integers (how else get a 2D grid?).

Anyway, I'm writing for two reasons. First, to vote for fixing this
bug :). Second, to ask for advice in working around it. I imagine I
could kluge something together with subplots, but is it possible to do
something nicer, like manually adjusting each facet's x-axis through
the low-level grid API? I don't know anything about grid, so if it is
possible, a concrete example would be useful.

Anyway, thanks for any advice. I love ggplot2, btw!
- Max

EXAMPLE FOLLOWS:

# my dump()ed dataframe:
example_data <-
structure(list(corpus = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
1L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L,
2L), .Label = c("buckeye", "children", "parents"), class = "factor"),
wordLen = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L
), .Label = c(">0 words", "3 words", "4 words", "5 words",
"6 words"), class = "factor"), property = structure(c(1L,
2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L,
1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L), .Label = c("assortMixByDeg",
"avgShortestPath", "clustCoeff", "edgeVertexRat",
"edgeVertexRatGC",
"giantCompPerc", "transitivity", "vertices"), class = "factor"),
mean = c(0.69928768069521, 5.6481782492839, 0.15525131141345,
1.7665108263423, 4.0703267529099, 0.39067951274847,
0.37207678461634,
6892.07, 0.7651415609009, 6.7099698963401, 0.21846931233901,
3.1664933843452, 5.2311479906582, 0.58443336014648,
0.40516321898728,
10092.51, 0.74687770938641, 5.4188678906388, 0.22495517832125,
2.9566104284035, 4.821001453467, 0.58099582309336,
0.41113979007947,
5612.48), sd = c(0.00469962352351303, 0.077420647604906,
0.00233987966367848, 0.0210387316747695, 0.0476063425324138,
0.00340480864546233, 0.0031276884380886, 37.1443417119232,
0.00445396655736635, 0.246486262747128, 0.00174799836180069,
0.0223489882265428, 0.0935795562694475, 0.0150931465716142,
0.00367334512129698, 32.185226236253, 0.00432979063197123,
0.0467362001102307, 0.00209010283752292, 0.0277554933820059,
0.0454530970664744, 0.00365226411841138, 0.00346423397416497,
22.0149077130966), samples = c(100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100,
100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100,
100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100)), .Names = c("corpus", "wordLen",
"property", "mean", "sd", "samples"), row.names = c(1L, 2L, 3L,
4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 41L, 42L, 43L, 44L, 45L, 46L, 47L, 48L, 81L,
82L, 83L, 84L, 85L, 86L, 87L, 88L), class = "data.frame")

# the plot
p <- qplot(mean, corpus, data=example_data, size=I(1.25))
p <- p + facet_grid(property ~ ., scales="free", space="free") # group
by prop
p <- p + opts(strip.text.y = theme_text()) # keep strip y label
horizontal
p <- p + labs(y = "Corpus", x = "Mean value plus/minus 2 standard
errors")
p <- p + opts(title = "Graph properties in 100 bootstrapped samples")
p <- p + opts(axis.title.y = theme_blank())

# error bars
p <- p + geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin=(mean-2*sd), xmax=(mean+2*sd),
height=0.2))
print(p)

--

Hi Max,

What's the problem? Facet_grid is behaving as expected here - it only
every has one horizontal scale per column and one vertical scale per
row. Perhaps you want this?

p + facet_wrap(~ property, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x")

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Workaround for broken scales = "free"?
parts:
Aha, yes, that does it, though I suppose it would be more tricky if I
had more than one column (and wanted the columns to correspond to some
variable).

I didn't realize that scales="free" for facet_grid would only give one
horizontal axis per column (and one vertical axis per row), rather
than free axes in each panel. If that's the intended behavior, that's
cool, but it should be better documented. help(facet_grid) only says
"You can also choose whether the scales should be constant across all
panels (the default), or whether they should be allowed to vary." That
wording suggests to me that scales="free" would allow scales to vary
across *all panels*, not just across columns/rows.

Anyway, thanks for the quick and helpful response!

-Max
